run: the ezafe voices check: over many unseen voices, does E5 keep the voice as well as E1
status: registered 2026-11-01, before any render of these voices
why: the ezafe check (eval/runs/persian-voice-omnivoice-ezafe-train.json, check_v1) heard E5 read best: 3 words wrong of 165 against E1's 6 and A1's 16, and picked best 8 times of 12. But on its one voice (mana) E5's held-out similarity was 0.023 below A1's with the interval wholly below zero, so it was flagged and not adopted, and 0.014 below E1's, [-0.027, -0.002]; it sat nearer the prompt clip itself (0.829 against E1's 0.818) and further from the speaker's other recordings. One voice and one seed, and the A run's step-5,000 export showed no such drop on its own check. On 2026-11-01 the user asked for it to be tested on many voices

voices.source: Neyshekar v6 (shekar-ai/neyshekar at 30696ada), its validation split: 26 speakers
voices.why_these: in no training split of the adaptation (their clips gave only its validation loss), not on OmniVoice's published list of training data, and never used to choose anything. texts.what: the ezafe check's twelve sentences as the app writes them - the tagger's ezafe, the homograph vowels, the number fixes - one text per sentence for every form. The dataset's tagger is switched off (VOICECLONE__TEXT__EZAFE__ENABLED=false) so its older code adds nothing: checked on this Mac, e1d96e4's text path passes all twelve unchanged, one chunk each

rendering: one Kaggle T4 x2 session on step 3's code dataset (e1d96e4), built by kaggle/build_ezafe_voices_kernel.py: scripts/benchmark.py once per form with --sentences-file, seed 42, each speaker's reference clip and its transcript; 25 x 12 = 300 renders per form, 900 in all. Held-out similarity (ECAPA against the four held-out clips) and CER are scored in the same session, the recogniser's floor by the first run. Every render's metadata must name the weights its form was given
rule: the app's OmniVoice weights become E5 if the 95% interval of E5's held-out similarity minus E1's - the mean of each speaker's paired differences, a t interval over speakers (scripts/compare_runs.py) - does not lie wholly below zero, and E5's mean CER is not more than 2 points above E1's. Otherwise they stay E1. An interval that cannot be given keeps E1
read_beside_it_not_for_the_decision: E1 and E5 against A1 the same way: if either lies wholly below zero it is said, and whether to go back to A1 is the user's call (the listening check heard A1 say 16 words wrong to E1's 6); every pair's CER; each interval beside compare_runs.py's practical reference of 0.0205
reading_code: scripts/read_ezafe_voices.py, with tests/test_read_ezafe_voices.py, written before any render
not_claimed: one seed; Neyshekar's read speech; similarity as ECAPA measures it; nobody listens in this check
cost: Kaggle: one session, about 3 h on the T4 pair (900 renders and their scoring) of this week's 30 h
